name: What is the difference between a pergola and a gazebo?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a pergola and a gazebo?

acceptedAnswer.text: While both pergolas and gazebos provide shade and define outdoor spaces, their structures differ. A pergola typically features an open, slatted roof supported by columns, offering partial shade and a framework for climbing plants. They are often integrated into existing structures or extend from a home. A gazebo, on the other hand, is a freestanding, often octagonal or round structure with a solid or semi-solid roof, providing more complete shade and shelter. Gazebos usually include built-in seating and create a more enclosed, private retreat within the garden.
acceptedAnswer.description: A pergola has an open, slatted roof offering partial shade, often attached, while a gazebo is a freestanding structure with a solid roof, providing more complete shelter.
